residencyRequirements.description: Either party must be (a) a citizen of Ghana, OR (b) domiciled in Ghana, OR (c) ordinarily resident in Ghana for at least 3 years immediately before filing (Matrimonial Causes Act 1971, s.31).

waitingPeriod.description: No mandatory waiting period after filing. The petitioner must inform the court of all efforts made to effect a reconciliation (MCA s.8(1)), and the court MAY adjourn the proceedings to attempt reconciliation where a reasonable possibility appears (s.8(2)) — referral is discretionary, not mandatory. No petition may be presented within two years of the marriage (MCA s.9(1)) except by leave of court (s.9(2)).

twoYearBar.description: No petition for divorce shall be presented to the court within two years of the date of the marriage (MCA s.9(1)). The court may grant leave on the ground of substantial hardship suffered by the petitioner or depravity on the part of the respondent (s.9(2)).

noFault.name: Separation with Consent (2 years)
noFault.description: The parties have not lived as man and wife for a continuous period of at least 2 years immediately preceding the presentation of the petition, and the respondent consents to the grant of a decree of divorce. Consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

noFault.name: Five-Year Separation
noFault.description: The parties have not lived as man and wife for a continuous period of at least 5 years immediately preceding the presentation of the petition. No consent from the respondent is required.

noFault.name: Inability to Reconcile After Diligent Effort
noFault.description: The parties to the marriage have, after diligent effort, been unable to reconcile their differences.

fault.name: Adultery and Intolerability
fault.description: The respondent has committed adultery and the petitioner finds it intolerable to live with the respondent.

fault.name: Unreasonable Behaviour
fault.description: The respondent has behaved in such a way that the petitioner cannot reasonably be expected to live with the respondent.

fault.name: Desertion (2 years)
fault.description: The respondent has deserted the petitioner for a continuous period of at least 2 years immediately preceding the filing.

ordinance.name: Ordinance Marriage
ordinance.description: Registered civil or church marriage under the Marriage Ordinance (Cap 127)

customary.name: Customary Marriage
customary.description: Marriage performed and recognized under customary law, may be registered under PNDCL 112

mohammedan.name: Mohammedan Marriage
mohammedan.description: Marriage performed under Islamic law and registered under the Marriage of Mohammedans Ordinance
mohammedan.statute: Marriages Act, 1884-1985 (CAP 127), Part Two (formerly Marriage of Mohammedans Ordinance, Cap 129)

basic.name: Petition for Divorce
basic.description: Initiates the divorce proceeding in the High Court under the Matrimonial Causes Act 1971

basic.name: Statement of Arrangements for Children
basic.description: Required if there are children of the marriage — details proposed custody and maintenance arrangements

basic.name: Affidavit in Support
basic.description: Sworn affidavit verifying the facts stated in the petition

reconciliation.description: The petitioner must inform the court of all efforts made to effect a reconciliation (MCA s.8(1)). Where a reasonable possibility of reconciliation appears, the court MAY adjourn the proceedings to enable an attempt at reconciliation (s.8(2)) — the referral is discretionary.

decreeProcess.description: The court grants a single decree of divorce. Under MCA s.37 every decree is final and takes effect from the date the court gives judgment — Ghana has no decree nisi / decree absolute stage.

legalCitations.description: Governs all divorce proceedings in Ghana — sole ground is that the marriage has broken down beyond reconciliation (s.1(2)), shown by the six facts in s.2(1)
Registration of customary marriages and divorces
Best interests of the child — custody, maintenance, and welfare
Spouse's property rights — equitable distribution on dissolution
Distribution of property on intestacy — relevant to spousal property entitlements
Criminalizes domestic violence and provides for protection orders

filingFees.notes: Court filing fees for a divorce petition range from approximately GHS 500 to GHS 1,000, depending on the court (High Court vs. Circuit Court) and the complexity of the case. Lawyer professional fees are separate and regulated by the Ghana Bar Association Scale of Legal Fees (2022), which typically ranges from GHS 30,000 to GHS 90,000. Indigent applicants may apply for a fee waiver.

childSupportGuidelines.notes: Ghana does not have a fixed formula for child maintenance. The court considers the needs of the child, the financial capacity of each parent, and the standard of living the child enjoyed during the marriage.

spousalSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may order either spouse to pay maintenance to the other. Factors include the duration of the marriage, the financial capacity and needs of each spouse, and whether either party contributed to the education or career of the other.

effectiveDateRule: The decree of divorce is final and takes effect from the date the court gives judgment (MCA s.37).
certificateNote: A Certificate of Divorce may be obtained from the High Court registry after the decree is granted.
